pages.text: "Dad, I want to sweep too!" Little brother Mumu ran toward the yard broom. Dad had just finished sweeping and stood it up. Big sister Dodo ran over and grabbed it too. "I want to sweep!"
"I got here first!" "No, me first!" Holding the handle, they pulled this way and that. Mumu wanted to sweep the whole yard alone. He shoved Dodo hard with a wing.
Thump! Dodo landed on her bottom. The broom fell beside her. Tears filled her eyes; Mumu's wing stung too. Nobody had the broom. They only felt upset.
Dad came and laid the broom between them. "Push with a wing, and your sister hurts and you don't get the broom. How about using words, not wings?" They looked at Dad.
"One, wings down! Two, speak with your beak!" Mumu spoke first. "Dodo, I wanted to sweep." She nodded. "Me too. What do we do?"
"Three, half each to sweep!" Dodo pointed a wing toward the straw pile. "Mumu, door to straw pile. Dodo, straw pile to bridge!" Dad put the broom in Mumu's wing.
Mumu's swept lines stretched from the door to the straw pile. "Your turn now!" He held out the broom. Taking it, Dodo called, "Use words, not wings!"
Dodo swept from the straw pile to the bridge. Together was much faster than alone. Mumu flicked his tail once.

Now Mumu knew three things. "One, wings down! Two, speak with my beak! Three, half each to sweep!" When they bumped by the water jar next day, he tucked his wings close. "Dodo, let's use our beaks to talk!"

Dad spread both wings around them. "Words make both of you smile, right?" Push with wings, and neither sweeps. Use words, and both sweep together. Looking at Dodo, Mumu called, "Use words, not wings!"
